claim: Nuclear patch-clamp electrophysiology enables the activities of single InsP3R channels to be recorded in their native ER membrane and luminal milieus.

evidence: Based on the methodology described in the manuscript

claim: The electrical currents through open InsP3R channels are overwhelmingly carried by K+ in patch-clamp electrophysiology experiments.
source: Because of the relatively low selectivity of InsP3R channels for Ca2+ vs K+ (15.2 : 1 [Vais et al., 2010a]) and orders of magnitude higher [K+] (140 mM) than that of other ions in the physiological solutions used in our experiments (70 nM to ≤600 μM [Ca2+]free; 0 or 200 μM [Mg2+]free), the electrical currents through open InsP3R channels are overwhelmingly carried by K+ in all our patch-clamp electrophysiology experiments, enabling the kinetics of channel gating to be studied with both luminal and cytoplasmic [Ca2+] well-defined and controlled.
evidence: Supported by citation to Vais et al., 2010a and logical inference from ion concentrations

claim: InsP3R channel activity can be modulated by [Ca2+]ER indirectly via feed-through effects of Ca2+ flux.
source: Using the nuclear patch-clamp approach in a previous study (Vais et al., 2012), we demonstrated that InsP3R channel activity can be modulated by [Ca2+]ER indirectly via feed-through effects of Ca2+ flux driven through an open channel by high [Ca2+]ER that raises the local [Ca2+]i in the channel vicinity to regulate its activity through its cytoplasmic activating and inhibitory Ca2+-binding sites (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study (Vais et al., 2012) and illustrated in Figure 2A

claim: Feed-through effects can be completely abrogated by sufficient Ca2+ chelation on the cytoplasmic side.
source: That study demonstrated that these feed-through effects can be completely abrogated by sufficient Ca2+ chelation on the cytoplasmic side to buffer local [Ca2+]i at cytoplasmic Ca2+ binding sites of the InsP3R.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study (Vais et al., 2012)

claim: In the presence of 5 mM diBrBAPTA on the cytoplasmic side, the open probability Po of the InsP3R channel did not change discernably when the [Ca2+]ER was switched between 70 nM and 300 μM.
source: In the presence of 5 mM 5,5'-diBromo BAPTA (a fast acting Ca2+ chelator) on the cytoplasmic side in the lum-out excised patch configuration (Figure 1B), the open probability Po of the InsP3R channel did not change discernably when the [Ca2+]ER was switched between 70 nM and 300 μM, no matter whether saturating 10 μM [InsP3] (Figure 2C in Vais et al., 2012) or sub-saturating 3 μM [InsP3] (Figure 7B in Vais et al., 2012) was present in the micropipette (2 μM [Ca2+]i was in the micropipette in all experiments described here).
evidence: Supported by citations to specific figures in Vais et al., 2012

claim: Switching [Ca2+]ER between 70 nM and 300 μM in lum-out excised membrane patches had no effect on channel activity when [Ca2+]free on the cytoplasmic side was well buffered.
source: Thus, as long as [Ca2+]free on the cytoplasmic side was well buffered, switching [Ca2+]ER between 70 nM and 300 μM in lum-out excised membrane patches had no effect on channel activity.
evidence: Based on experimental data described in the manuscript
